previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer and a history of gastroparesis was admitted with severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had been recently discharged after a similar admission and was found to have hypokalemia, acidosis, and a urinary tract infection resistant to her outpatient antibiotic, which was treated with IV ceftriaxone. During the hospitalization, she developed C. difficile colitis, requiring oral vancomycin. Her long-acting morphine was adjusted due to concerns about worsening gastroparesis, and she opted to delay GJ tube placement until an outpatient procedure. She improved with IV fluids, antiemetics, and symptom management, and was discharged home on oral medications with follow-up planned for oncology and gastroenterology.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with gastroparesis, NG placed prior to GJ tube
placement// NG tube placement verification

TECHNIQUE:  Portable supine abdominal radiograph was obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis ___

FINDINGS: 

Port-A-Cath terminates in the cavoatrial junction.  An nasogastric tube
terminates at the height of the gastroesophageal junction, advancement of at
least 7 cm is recommended for optimal positioning.  An Amplatzer device is new
since prior CT from ___ and projects over the midline.  Surgical
clips are seen in the left and right upper quadrants and left axilla.

Lung volumes are low.   Bilateral horizontal linear opacities may reflect
subsegmental atelectasis.  Cardiomediastinal hilar silhouettes are within
normal limits.

There are no abnormally dilated loops of large or small bowel in the upper
abdomen.
Supine assessment limits detection for free air; there is no gross
pneumoperitoneum.
Osseous structures are unremarkable with the exception of a right total
shoulder arthroplasty.

IMPRESSION:


1. Nasogastric tube terminates at the height of the gastroesophageal junction,
advancement of approximately 7 cm is recommended for optimal positioning.
2. New Amplatzer device in place.
3. No acute intrathoracic findings.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with severe gastroparesis with previous gj tube
now with severe nausea requires a gj tube again for nutrition// Gj tube
placement

COMPARISON:  ___ percutaneous GJ tube check

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, attending Interventional Radiologist
and Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology fellow, and Dr. ___
___, interventional radiology resident performed the procedure. Dr. ___
___ supervised the trainee during any key components of the procedure
where applicable and reviewed and agrees with the findings as reported below.

ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
150mcg of fentanyl and 3 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 65 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: 1 mg glucagon IV, 1 g Ceftriazone IV
CONTRAST: 25 ml of Optiray contrast
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  37.5 minute, 159 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Placement of a 16 ___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

A scout image of the abdomen was obtained. The stomach was insufflated through
the indwelling nasogastric tube. Using a marker, the skin was marked using
palpation to feel the costal margins and the liver edge was marked using
ultrasound.

Under fluoroscopic guidance, 3 T fastener buttons were sequentially deployed
in a triangular position elevating the stomach to the anterior abdominal wall.
Intra-gastric position was confirmed with aspiration of air and injection of
contrast. A 19 gauge needle was introduced under fluoroscopic guidance and
position confirmed using an injection of dilute contrast. The needle
trajectory was directed towards the pylorus. A ___ wire was introduced and
coiled within the stomach.  A small skin incision was made along the needle
and the needle was removed.

A sheath was place and a Kumpe catheter was then introduced over the wire and
the ___ was exchanged for a Glidewire. The Glidewire and a Kumpe cathter
was used to advance the wire into the ___ part of the duodenum.  The sheath
was then removed and a peel-away sheath was placed over the wire. A 16 ___
MIC gastrojejunostomy catheter was advanced over the wire into position. The
sheath was then peeled away.

The wire and sheath were removed. The catheter was locked by inflating the
gastric balloon in the stomach after confirming the position of the catheter
with a contrast injection. The catheter was then flushed and capped.  Sterile
dressings were applied. The patient tolerated the procedure well and there
were no immediate complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. Successful placement of a 16 ___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube with its tip
in the proximal jejunum.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a 16 ___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube with its tip in
the proximal jejunum. The gastric port should not be used for 24 hours.
